q2_gaps: an explicit quantifier word ('no') on the OBJECT of a verbal generic: the QuantifierPhrase companion shape (QuantifierPhrase <kind> <verb-lemma> "<word>") names only the quantified subject range, so there is no licensed carrier for object-position 'no' and 'need no salt-bloom' becomes indistinguishable from 'do not need salt-bloom'
notes: The proper-noun premodifier is correctly routed to opaque Possession (possessed first) and carried as a premise conjunct on the distributing rule, as an adjectivally-restricted kind subject would be; stative 'need' takes Experiencer/Stimulus by the progressive test, salt_bloom gets its head genus only (noun modifier never exposed), and the negated verbal generic sits at (STV 0.0 0.9). Omitting the QuantifierPhrase is defensible here because the rule quantifies lanterns rather than salt_bloom, but the surface quantifier is then unrecorded anywhere in the parse.
